output.reason: An 8-year-old with right ear pain since last night, no reported fever, eating normally and attending school can start with home comfort measures and observation, with clinician review if pain persists or new warning features appear.
output.patientMessage: You can manage this at home for now: give age-appropriate pain relief as directed on the package, and a warm cloth over the ear can help. Ear pain like this often settles within a couple of days. Message us for clinician review if the pain lasts beyond 2-3 days, worsens, or fluid drains from the ear. Seek in-person care today if she develops fever, swelling, redness or tenderness behind the ear, an ear that sticks out, neck stiffness, or she becomes drowsy or unwell.
differential: Acute otitis media or middle ear effusion
Otitis externa or referred pain from throat/teeth

redFlags.concern: Ill or toxic appearance / reduced intake
redFlags.quote: she ate breakfast fine and went to school

redFlags.concern: Postauricular swelling, redness or protruding ear (mastoiditis)
Neck stiffness or altered mental status

output.vitalSigns: No temperature or other vital-sign readings were reported; the parent stated "No fever" but whether any measurement was taken is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: No ear examination findings are available, so the cause of the pain is unconfirmed and cited AOM data may not apply.

citations.claim: Most acute otitis media episodes are self-limited, supporting initial symptomatic care and observation.
citations.limitation: No otoscopy, so AOM is not confirmed in this child; ED reference synthesis, not a telehealth protocol.

citations.claim: Postauricular swelling, tenderness and erythema with fever suggest mastoiditis and require urgent evaluation, supporting the safety-net advice.
